highlights.title: Stop repeated forecast and Carbs Required alerts
changes: Forecast (Low Glucose Soon) and Carbs Required alarms no longer re-trigger on every loop when a CGM app owns glucose‑by.
Only alarms driven by the current CGM reading are handed off to the CGM app when that option is enabled.
Forecast and Carbs Required alerts now remain active until they recover or are snoozed, instead of being cleared and re.
Alert behavior around CGM-owned readings is now more consistent and avoids duplicate notifications.

highlights.title: Prevent freeze when editing carb entries
changes: Editing a carb entry no longer sometimes hangs the app when switching back to the chart.
Saved carb edits no longer risk deleting the entry if an internal recalculation fails.
Chart updates are more stable because redundant internal updates are skipped.
Chart performance is improved when many basal segments are shown, reducing slowdowns.

highlights.title: Immediate update of glucose app badge
changes: Turning off Show Glucose App Badge removes the number from the app icon immediately.
Changing glucose units refreshes the app badge right away.

includedPullRequests.title: Keep forecast and carbs-required alarms firing when the CGM owns glucose alerts
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

When **Use CGM App Alerts** is on and the active CGM provides its own glucose alerts (Dexcom G5/G6/G7, Libre, xDrip4iOS — the default on those), `GlucoseAlertCoordinator.evaluateGlucoseAlarms()` bails out on every new reading and called `retractAllFiringIfNeeded()`. That retracted **every** firing alarm, including **Low Glucose Soon** (`forecastedLow`) and **Carbs Required** (`carbsRequired`), which are determination-driven and deliberately *not* covered by the CGM-ownership guard (#1428: a CGM app can alarm on the current reading, but it cannot compute Trio's oref forecast or `carbsReq`).

A few seconds later the loop's determination re-evaluated them, found the condition still true, saw no entry in `firingAlertIDs`, and fired again — a fresh notification with sound and a new in-app banner on **every loop cycle**, for as long as the forecast (or `carbsReq`) stayed past threshold. The 5-minute `AlertThrottler` never engaged, because `retractAlert` resets it.

This became visible with #1428 (before it, Low Glucose Soon never fired at all on these CGMs). Carbs Required has had the same behaviour since the user-configurable alarm list landed.

## Fix

On the reading path, retract only the alarms whose `type.isReadingDriven` is true — the ones the CGM app is actually covering. Forecast and carbs-required alarms keep their firing state across reading updates and are retracted where they always were: by their own evaluators on recovery (threshold + `recoveryMarginMgDL`) or on snooze.

The filter is a static pure helper, `alarmsToRetractWhenCGMOwnsAlerts(firing:in:)`, next to the existing `breached` / `shouldRetract` helpers, following this file's pattern for testable predicates (the coordinator itself is Swinject-injected). `retractAllFiringIfNeeded()` had no other caller and is removed.

## Evidence from a real device

Dexcom G7, **Use CGM App Alerts** on, one Low Glucose Soon alarm enabled.

**Same day, same device, same alarm — before and after the fix.** The build was swapped mid-day; these are the `TrioAlertManager.issueAlert` times for one `forecastedLow` alarm id (UTC):

- **Before the fix** (05:33–08:51): `05:33, 05:51, 05:56, 06:01, 06:06, 06:11, 06:16, 06:21, 06:26, 06:31, 06:36, 06:41, 06:46, 06:51, 06:56, 07:01, 07:06, 07:11, 07:16, 07:21, 07:26, 07:31, 07:36, 07:46, 07:51, 08:01, 08:21, 08:41, 08:46, 08:51` — 30 alerts, one per loop cycle, for over three hours of a single low-forecast episode.
- **After the fix** (12:46–23:59): `12:46, 15:56, 16:31, 17:51, 19:16` — 5 alerts, each a separate episode.

**One week of logs**, gap between consecutive issues of the same alarm id:

| | consecutive pairs | ≤ 6 min apart | median gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low Glucose Soon — before | 49 | 40 (82%) | **5 min** |
| Low Glucose Soon — after | 52 | **0 (0%)** | **90 min** |
| Carbs Required — before | 30 | 25 (83%) | **5 min** |
| Carbs Required — after | 40 | **0 (0%)** | **135 min** |

Three things worth noting in that table:

1. Nothing fires at loop cadence any more — not one pair inside 6 minutes, against ~82% before.
2. The alarms are not silenced: there are *more* issues after the fix (52 and 40 pairs over seven days) than before (49 and 30 over two). Each one is a distinct breach episode.
3. Because a re-fire requires the alarm to have been retracted first, that also demonstrates recovery → re-breach still works — the fix does not leave alarms stuck in `firingAlertIDs`.

Reading-driven alarms (`low` / `urgentLow` / `high`) stayed at **0 issues** throughout, before and after, so CGM-ownership suppression of the reading path is intact. No `throttled` lines in the whole window, so every issue above was a real delivery rather than a suppressed duplicate.

## Reproduction

Any CGM in `CGMManagerAlertOwnership` (Dexcom G5/G6/G7, Libre, xDrip4iOS) with "Use CGM App Alerts" left on, one enabled Low Glucose Soon alarm, and a forecast whose minimum across the IOB/COB/UAM/ZT curves at +20 min stays at or below the threshold for more than one loop cycle. Expected: one alert until recovery or snooze. Actual: the notification is removed and re-posted with sound on every cycle. Easiest to see with Carbs Required set to a low gram threshold.

## Tests

Three tests added to the existing `CGMOwnershipSuppressionScopeTests` suite: a mixed firing set returns only `urgentLow`/`low`/`high` in input order; a reading-driven alarm that is not firing is excluded; an empty firing set returns nothing. They cover the predicate rather than the queue bookkeeping, as with the other tests in that file.

SwiftFormat lint clean with the project's rule set.

## Note on scope

This does not change #1428's decision that forecast alarms stay armed under CGM ownership — it only stops the reading path from clearing them. One consequence of #1428 that this makes more visible: with the reading path suppressed, `lowFamilyFiring` in `evaluateForecast` is always false, so Trio's "may go below X in 20 min" can sit alongside the CGM app's own actual-low alarm. That was already the case and is orthogonal to this fix.

includedPullRequests.title: fix: prevent UI freeze when editing a carb entry
includedPullRequests.body:
Fixes an issue when editing a carb entry: the app could hang when switching back to the chart.

Steps to reproduce the issue: 
Open Meals History -> Edit a carb entry -> Click Save -> Quickly switch to the chart. Repeat 5-10 times (the issue is sporadic). More likely to reproduce on complex fat/protein meals.

### Freeze explanation: 
MainChartCanvas recomputes derived basal state and assigns it to @State unconditionally, which invalidates the body and triggers another recompute. Three things kept the cycle from settling: preparedTempBasals held tuples (not Equatable, so @State can never skip a redundant update); calculateTempBasals and calculateBasals each derived values from a fresh Date() (sub-microsecond resolution), so results did not compare equal; and neither assignment checked whether the value had changed.

basalDomainMax is now cached instead of rescanning both series once per mark, which was quadratic in segment count.

### Testing:
Tested on iPhone 15, iOS26 — the device we use for Trio.
Repeated edit/delete cycles, simple and complex (fat/protein) meals. 
Added Self._printChanges() logging to confirm _preparedTempBasals went from unbounded to 3 evaluations per session.

includedPullRequests.title: Refresh glucose app badge when settings change
includedPullRequests.body:
Turning off Show Glucose App Badge did not remove the number from the app icon until the next glucose reading came in, or until Trio was restarted. This came up in a Facebook support thread where a user could not get rid of the badge and others suggested force closing the app.

The notifications manager now listens for settings changes and refreshes the badge immediately, so turning it on or off and switching units take effect right away.
